mathematical_repairs: Alteration and birational reflection scopes distinguish Cartier approximants from general homogeneous psh functions; finite bijections have fibrewise-constant image.
Raw nonflat finite maps are separated from their constant-rank flatifications; Frobenius weights and characteristic-two cone weights belong to finite-flat scopes.
Largest target quasi-finite open and universal properness cancellation are justified; de Jong regular/smooth/projective and finite-ground-field conditions are explicit.
Stein first-factor birationality requires generic finiteness. The normal middle term comes from the normal source, with relative-normalization hypotheses checked.

Numerical pullback uses the curve projection formula; integral degree ledgers, curve lifts, nefness and effective rational Cartier cone pullbacks are verified without unrestricted Cartier-class pushforward.
A reverse-order factorization, when it exists, can be normalized with already available finite normalization; source/target normality and EP assumptions are mapped correctly.
The explicit surface supremum has poles despite being FS; its zero carrier and domination are checked. Exceptional section orders are computed in a vertex frame, not inferred from a numerical class.

Characteristic-two finite-free charts cover the whole map; trace and Reynolds section operators are distinguished from logarithmic norm averaging, and nonreduced group-scheme possibilities are not excluded.
The global inseparable norm section is identified by its divisor and norm line before using its local coefficient. Full field-degree/Artin-length weights retain possible defect.
The drifting FS sequence increases at one point and is not a decreasing regularization; an explicitly known birational pullback can be transferred to finite norm data.
General psh polar sets, arbitrary-function usc pullback, proof boundaries and node/cusp counterexample attributions are limited to what the cited arguments establish.
Unsupported novelty and whole-input verification claims are removed; named de Jong, Stein, RG, ideal and homogeneous Siu foundations remain explicit.
